name: FL-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Open Republican-held seat in an R+14 district
Schwartzel's roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage over Arias
Prediction markets price the Republican near 94%
No public polling; open-seat dynamics add some uncertainty
model.rationale: An R+14 open seat, a roughly 40-to-1 fundraising gap favoring the Republican, and markets pricing the GOP near 94% all point the same direction; with no polling suggesting competition, a double-digit Republican margin is the clear call.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected Republican stumble could pull the margin toward single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving this southwest Florida seat to run for governor, but the district's strong Republican lean remains. The partisan lean is R+14, and even with the seat open, the expected margin is a solid double digit for the GOP. No public general-election polls are available, so the picture rests on fundamentals, money, and markets.

Republican Jim Schwartzel has raised about $2.8 million and holds more than $500,000 on hand, while Democrat Victor Arias has raised roughly $70,000 with little cash remaining. Prediction markets put Republican win odds near 94%, and an independent candidate trails far behind in fundraising. Everything points to the seat staying in Republican hands; the main uncertainty comes from the lack of polling and the usual volatility of an open-seat contest.
